text:
zoe: ALB started removing edge targets in eu-west-1 around 08:12 UTC — ALB logs show healthcheck connections being RSTed. Targets go UNHEALTHY then deregistered. Anyone seeing this across clusters?

arjun: yep saw spikes during a GPU node provisioning wave. Lots of short outbound connections from pods/sidecars to model-registry and metrics, wondering if ephemeral port churn is colliding with SNAT mapping.

kai: pulling logs — sample ALB access line:```
2026-03-17T08:12:14Z alb-request 3.4.5.6:56789 10.1.2.3:8080 GET /health HTTP/1.1 200 - 0 2 0 123 0 \"connection reset by peer\"
```Looks like probe reached pod, app answered, then TCP reset happened quickly.

net-bot: ALERT: conntrack_utilization on egress-nat-1 = 98% -> drops increasing (count=432)

sara: ran quick checks on a node affected by deregistration:```sh
# count TIME_WAIT sockets
ss -tn state time-wait | wc -l
12034
# ephemeral ports in use (approx)
ess -tn sport :32768-60999 | wc -l
9500
```Lots of TIME_WAIT from transient connections.

arjun: hypothesis: when NAT source ports are exhausted we get port reuse and the ALB healthcheck connection ends up being translated to an existing flow (TIME_WAIT), which causes the backend to RST or the response to map to a different flow. Combined with short probe intervals this looks like target evict.

zoe: proposed immediate mitigations: 1) enable HTTP keepalive in sidecar for registry/metrics to reduce new TCP creation 2) ask networking to expand SNAT port allocation / add another NAT gateway placement for egress distribution 3) increase ALB healthcheck timeout to 10s and unhealthy threshold to 3 so transient resets don't evict quickly.

kai: rolling a tiny canary of the sidecar keepalive tweak now (pooling + keepalive=60s) to 5 pods in edge-asg-3. Will report if healthchecks stabilize.

sara: net team: temporarily added an extra NAT gateway behind the egress TG and bumped conntrack hashsize on the affected nodes. conntrack drops dropped to 0 in the last 90s.

net-bot: INFO: conntrack_utilization on egress-nat-1 = 42% -> stable

arjun: good. longer term we should: - add a preflight check when doing large GPU provisioning to protect ephemeral port availability - instrument per-ENI ephemeral port headroom - move non-critical telemetry to UDP or buffered aggregation - add a dedicated egress path for healthchecks to avoid SNAT collapse.

zoe: action items: @net-team open ticket to formalize NAT autoscale and per-region port headroom; @infra reduce healthcheck aggressiveness for edge target groups; @devex roll keepalive change to all sidecars in next rollout. I'll create the follow-up tickets.

kai: canary looks good so far, 0 target removals in the 10min window after patch. :thumbsup:

sara: leaving the extra NAT in place for the next 4 hours while we monitor metrics.

zoe: thanks all — tagging as resolved-for-now, will track the follow-ups in tickets.
